newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-NAGANO AGREES TO GAMES EMERGENCY COUNCIL.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NAGANO AGREES TO GAMES EMERGENCY COUNCIL.

text.p: An emergency council of Olympic officials and organisers will meet early each morning during next year's Nagano Winter Olympics to assess weather conditions and recommend scheduling changes, a Nagano Olympic official said on Monday.

The council was set up in response to a request last week from the executive board of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to ensure flexibility, said Naokichi Nishimura, deputy director general of the Nagano organising committee.

IOC vice-president Marc Hodler said the council would consist of IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch, chief Nagano organiser Makoto Kobayashi and representatives from the Games three biggest television rights holders, the American network CBS, the European Broadcasting Union and Japan's NHK.
Hodler, who doubles as president of the International Ski Federation (FIS), said the concept was borrowed from skiing, which must constantly deal with changeable weather conditions.
"The ski federation always had this type of council because we always have risks with the weather, so we wanted the same with the Olympics," said Hodler.
